profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility is located at 4514 Chester Avenue, Cleveland, OH 44103, in Cuyahoga County; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Cuyahoga County has moved proactively on data center policy: the county released a Data Center Development Guide for municipalities in June 2026, recommending scrutiny of power and water demand, grid-upgrade costs, backup generators, job creation, and decommissioning plans, and advising local officials to decline signing non-disclosure agreements with data center developers. County Executive Chris Ronayne said the county owes it to residents "to stop bad deals before they start," citing a rejected $1.6 billion hyperscale proposal in Cleveland's Slavic Village neighborhood; Cleveland City Council separately held a hearing in late June 2026 on a proposed city moratorium. This local scrutiny sits alongside Ohio's broader statewide data center tax exemption, which cost $554.9 million in 2024 and $1.57 billion in 2025, far exceeding original forecasts, per Signal Ohio.

reading.body:
This facility's published specifications do not include information about power capacity, IT load, cooling infrastructure, or supported workload types. Without these figures, no assessment is possible of its compute density, expansion potential, or role in AI infrastructure scaling.

Lumen Cleveland is one of three numbered Lumen facilities in Cleveland, Ohio, and the registry cannot distinguish which physical building this entry refers to based on available sources. The address field contains a candidate location, but research notes indicate three separate facilities with confirmed distinct addresses, and coordinates alone did not resolve to a single building.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, but only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 60.4 megawatts across the state. This facility's rank of ninth by published megawatts indicates it either publishes no capacity figure or is listed without a specification this site has read. The state context shows that most mapped facilities in Ohio do not publicly disclose power specifications.
